annotations.title: Read a North Carolina (NC) session law, by act-section

description:
The text of North Carolina (NC) session laws — the enacted acts — by act-section.

Use when an answer turns on what an ACT says rather than the codified statute: "what does
Sec. 5.14 of S.L. 2026-61 do", an uncodified "Notwithstanding G.S. 143-129 …" provision,
an amendment to one subsection the codified text has not caught up with, or when an act
takes effect. get_statute names acts touching a section; this reads them.

- `session_law` alone: the act's title, effective date, the chapters it creates or
  repeals, and its table of contents (each act-section's number, caption and the G.S.
  sections it names), paged by `limit`/`offset`.
- `session_law` + `section`: the full text of that act-section ("5.14" gives 5.14.(a),
  (b), …).
- `citation` (a G.S. section), with or without `session_law`: every provision naming it,
  newest act first.
- `query`: provisions containing all the words, in one act or across all of them.

Amended text is marked as the act prints it: [-deleted-] {+inserted+}. Covers the acts
of the current biennium (2025-) that ncleg has published; a bill not yet law is not
here. This is the act's own text, not the codified statute — use get_statute for that.

citation.description: A G.S. section: return the act provisions that name it — amendments of one subsection, uncodified "Notwithstanding G.S. …" provisions, effective-date clauses. Without `session_law`, searches every act.

limit.description: Maximum entries (1-50): act-sections in an act's contents, or provisions found by `citation` or `query`.

max_chars.description: Total characters of provision text in the answer (default 15000). A cut provision says so.

offset.description: Skip this many act-sections of an act's contents; pass the previous answer's `next_offset`.

query.description: Words that must all appear in the provision. Within `session_law` when given, else across every act.

section.description: An act-section number as the act prints it. "5.14" returns every lettered part (5.14.(a), (b), …); "5.14(a)" one of them.

session_law.description: The act, as "S.L. 2026-61", "Session Law 2026-61" or "2026-61". May carry its section: "S.L. 2026-61, s. 5.14" or "Sec. 5.14 of S.L. 2026-61".
